recentItems.title: 1985: Parkinson - Professional Yorkshireman? | Harty Goes to Yorkshire | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
The War of the Roses comes to the mining village of Cudworth near Barnsley, as native Lancastrian Russell Harty meets Yorkshireman Michael Parkinson, for a trip back to his roots.

Will Harty fall prey to the delights of bitter beer, street cricket, Oakwell Stadium, and the back row of The Rock cinema? Will Parky finally get his dream interview 'with the bloke who pinched my bike in 1954'?


Clip taken from Harty Goes to... Yorkshire, originally broadcast on BBC Two, 13 October, 1985.

recentItems.title: 1974: Earning some extra pocket money | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
“We used to get about 90 pence for three hours work…”

Young reporter Edward Conley finds out how kids earn a bit of extra pocket money, and it’s not all paper rounds and babysitting. Amongst those earning whilst learning, are a teenage comedian working the North-West club circuit, and two boys in Bleasby who have undergone a medical to keep up their litter-picking work.


Clip taken from Search, originally broadcast on BBC One, 16 January 1974.

recentItems.title: 1965: Is Women's Wrestling Wrong? | Tonight | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
"These are tough maidens... you can't fix the floor - that stays hard, routines or no routines."

Fyfe Robertson reports on a women's wrestling match between Mitzi Mueller and “Naughty” Nancy Barton, at the Victoria Hall in Halifax. The match is the first ever all-in women's wrestling match that Halifax has ever seen, and if the Victoria Hall committee get their way, it will be the last. 

Fyfe questions Councillor Thomas Enderbury, the Chairmman of the hall committee, about what specific objections the committee has to women's wrestling. He also speaks to some of the spectators in attendance about their thoughts on women wrestling, and finally to Mitzi and Nancy themselves.


Clip taken from Tonight, originally broadcast on BBC One, 26 January, 1965.

recentItems.title: 1975: Lesley Judd Visits Bishop Rock Lighthouse | Blue Peter | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
"A day that I'll never forget for the rest of my life!"

Blue Peter's Lesley Judd pays an eventful visit to the isolated Bishop Rock lighthouse - four miles away from anything else in the Atlantic ocean. Lesley travels to the lighthouse aboard a boat skippered by the experienced Mike Hicks and, as Mike navigates the roiling seas around the base of the lighthouse, Lesley is winched onto Bishop Rock using a breeches buoy.

Once inside the lighthouse, principal keeper Andy Bluer shows her around, explaining how the light itself works and is maintained. After a very brief visit, Lesley has to make another nerve-wracking winch trip back down onto the waiting boat.


Clip taken from Blue Peter, originally broadcast on BBC One, 4 December, 1975.

recentItems.title: 1982: A Nuclear Bomb in London | Q.E.D.: A Guide to Armageddon | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
*WARNING: This film contains distressing scenes. Viewers may find this film frightening and upsetting*

"Maybe the most important television programme ever networked in Britain" - The Daily Telegraph

"In the coolest, most measured terms, accompanied by exceptionally skilled special effects and filmed and edited with the utmost precision, Mick Jackson's programme builds a cumulative portrait of horror, whose impact might well prove more lasting than any fictionalised or dramatised version." - The Guardian

An examination of the effects of nuclear weapons. The programme looks at the physical effects of a single, medium-sized nuclear warhead on a large city. How effectively would various types of shelter protect us from these effects?


Clip taken from Q.E.D. - A Guide to Armageddon, originally broadcast on BBC One, 26 July, 1982.

recentItems.title: 1997: The People Who Paint Pylons | Picture This | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
Each year, from March to October, 250 painters set about the task of painting the nation's electricity pylons. The work is uncomfortable and carries considerable health risks. Kirkham Jackson's film follows a team of four painters who remain undeterred by the hazards of their profession.


Clip taken from Picture This: Silvering Up, originally broadcast on BBC Two, 20 October, 1997.

recentItems.title: 1976: The Dartford Tunnel is Skint | Nationwide | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
"Where Kent clasps Essex in a concrete handshake, ninety feet beneath the Thames."

Luke Casey reports on the second Dartford tunnel, which has been under construction for over two years at a vast cost, and is two years behind schedule. This, together with outstanding debts incurred in constructing the first tunnel, has led to the toll being doubled. The doubling of the toll has led to a reduction in traffic, which could in turn mean that there is insufficient demand for the second tunnel. What can be done?


Clip taken from Nationwide, originally broadcast on BBC One, 15 September, 1976.

recentItems.title: 1967: Test Drive a "Driving Simulator" | Blue Peter | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
John Noakes and Valerie Singleton demonstrate Auto Tutor, a new driving simulator - "a car you can drive without moving an inch" - that has been designed as a driving aid for learner drivers.

They then take part in a simulated driving competition, under the watchful eyes of the acclaimed racing driver Graham Hill. 


Clip taken from Blue Peter, originally broadcast on BBC One, 6 November, 1967.

recentItems.title: 1979: Bad Banjo Player, Great Banjo Collector | Nationwide | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
Tony Wilkinson reports on Reuben Reubens, an avid collector of hundreds of banjos who, ironically, can't find time to learn how to play one. Poor Doreen.

Fortunately, Nationwide have provided a banjo player, Dave Firth, to demonstrate how some of Reuben's banjo collection should sound.


Clip taken from Nationwide, originally broadcast on BBC One, 28 March, 1979.
